Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No documented integration of electoral register with the interoperability platform. CNIE is used as a voter registration document but no API-level data exchange between electoral commission and data exchange hub documented. Score 2: planned within broader interoperability agenda.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) was accompanied by a comment suggesting a score of 2 (Planned) — an internal inconsistency. The two cited sources (a 2022 wearetech.africa piece on the ADD e-government interoperability platform, and a dig.watch summary of Digital Morocco 2030) are generic and do not specifically address electoral register integration; fetched both and confirmed neither mentions the electoral register or CNIE-based electoral verification. Fresh search found Ministry of Interior Decision No. 503.26 (13 March 2026, published in the Bulletin Officiel), implementing Law No. 57.11, which launched www.listeselectorales.ma — an online voter-registration platform letting citizens check enrolment and polling-station assignment using their CNIE (electronic national ID) number, ahead of the September 2026 legislative elections (corroborated by lemaroc360.com and lematin.ma, both March 2026). This shows genuine progress on electoral-register digitisation and CNIE-based identity verification, but there is no evidence the platform is connected to Morocco's central interoperability/data exchange hub run by the Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD), as opposed to being a standalone Ministry of Interior system. Given this ambiguity over what counts as 'integration with the data exchange' under this variable's definition, flagged for human review rather than asserting an upgraded code; a reviewer may wish to consider code 2 (Planned) or 3 (Under development) in light of the new 2026 evidence.
revised_comments: Morocco's electoral register is managed through the Ministry of Interior's online platform (listeselectorales.ma), launched under Decision No. 503.26 (March 2026) implementing Law No. 57.11. The platform allows voters to register, check their enrolment status, and find their assigned polling station by entering their CNIE (electronic national identity card) number together with their surname or date of birth, providing CNIE-based identity verification for electoral purposes. There is no publicly documented evidence that electoral register data is exchanged through Morocco's central government interoperability platform, operated by the Agence de Développement du Digital, which supports systems such as the Single Social Register and the MASSAR school management system. Electoral data instead appears to sit within a dedicated Ministry of Interior information system.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Morocco has the National Commission for Personal Data Protection (CNDP) established 2009. Right of Access to Information Law (No. 31-13) promotes transparency and accountability. Open Data Watch ranking: 35th globally (2022). Digital Morocco 2030 includes transparency provisions and citizen engagement. Public procurement portal publishes contract awards and tender notices. ADD publishes some activity reporting. Score 3: moderate/annual reports.

revision_notes: Fetched all three original sources. cndp.ma confirms the CNDP remains active and operating under Law 09-08. trade.gov confirms Law No. 31-13 (Right of Access to Information), Law 53-05 (Electronic Data Exchange) and the interoperability legislation. dig.watch confirms the Digital Morocco 2030 strategy's e-government axis. These support the general transparency context but do not, on their own, evidence annual reporting specific to the data exchange platform. Supplementary search found the World Bank ENNAJAA Program-for-Results appraisal document, which confirms the ADD publishes a national Open Data portal (data.gov.ma, with a published target of 245 datasets), conducts periodic user-satisfaction surveys on the interoperability platform, and reports disaggregated data-quality results — plus infomediaire.net (Feb 2024) reporting that ADD's governing board publicly approved its 2024 action plan and reviewed 2021-2023 activity and accounts. This is consistent with the original 'Moderate = Annual Reports' scoring rather than a full public dashboard. Score of 3 confirmed; only the Value Name's cosmetic mismatch with the scale label was noted, no change needed.
revised_comments: Morocco has an active data protection authority, the CNDP (Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel, established under Law 09-08 in 2009), and a Right of Access to Information Law (Law No. 31-13) that underpins transparency and accountability in public administration. Under the World Bank-supported ENNAJAA programme, the Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) operates a national Open Data portal (data.gov.ma) publishing several hundred datasets, and conducts periodic user-satisfaction surveys and data-quality assessments on the national interoperability platform. The ADD's governing board also publicly approves and reports on its annual action plan and budget, with summaries covered in the domestic press. This amounts to a moderate level of transparency, characterised by annual reporting and an open data portal, rather than a dedicated real-time public dashboard for the data exchange platform itself.
